name: Cimmerian-Machair
description: Rock deserts and sand seas take turns under a sky like hammered brass. Between dust events the wind redraws an ancient meteor crater, patient as erosion itself.
The air carries wet iron and lichen, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
There is money in silicon and solar potential and history in the rocks, and the two keep interfering with each other. Mediators do brisk business at inflated rates.
